title: Combe Hay Locks Circular Walk Route

images.title: Robert Powell, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Combe Hay Locks, Somerset Coal Canal. Combe Hay was the site of a series of locks, dating from 1805 on the Somerset Coal Canal on which research and restoration is proposed. It is the site of one of the only caisson locks ever built which was near the current Caisson House. Many of the locks and associated workings are listed buildings. It was also served by the Camerton and Limpley Stoke Railway.

description: This circular walk explores the area around the Somerset villages of Combe Hay and Southstoke. On the way you will visit the Somerset Coal Canal and the old Combe Hay Locks which is now a dry lock. There's fine views across to the surrounding countryside of the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. There's also the option to stop off in neighbouring Southstoke for rest and refreshments.
